description_ru: Вымышленная новость: после восьми месяцев ремонта в городе Эшфорд-Грин открыли старый каменный мост.
text:
After eight months of work, the old stone bridge in the town of Ashford Green opened again on Monday morning. Hundreds of people came to watch the ceremony, and many of them were smiling. The bridge, which is almost two hundred years old, crosses the River Lenn, and it is the only direct road between the two parts of the town.

The story began last winter. In February, heavy rain made the river much higher and faster than usual, and an inspector found large cracks in the stone. The council closed the bridge immediately, because it was too dangerous for cars and buses. For the next eight months, people had to drive eleven kilometres around the town to reach the other side. A journey that normally took five minutes suddenly took half an hour.

The closed bridge made life difficult for everyone. Children could not walk to school with their friends. Elderly people had to take two buses to go to the doctor. Shopkeepers on Market Street lost many customers, because people went to the big supermarket near the motorway instead. "It was the worst winter for my business," said Linda Okafor, who owns a small bakery. "On some days, I sold only ten loaves of bread. Usually I sell more than a hundred."

The repair work was harder than the engineers expected. First, they had to build a temporary wall in the water and pump out the river. Then they removed more than four hundred damaged stones and replaced them with new ones that were cut in a local quarry. They wanted to keep the old look of the bridge, so each stone was cut by hand. The engineer in charge, Peter Halloran, said that the work was like a big puzzle. "Some stones were broken in the middle, and some had moved by ten centimetres," he explained. "We worked in rain, snow and wind."

In June, there was another problem. A family of swans built a nest in the middle of the work area, and the workers were not allowed to disturb them. For three weeks, the engineers worked on the other side of the bridge. Local children visited the nest every day and gave the swans names. When the baby swans were born, the whole town celebrated. "It was the cutest delay in history," said Mr Halloran with a laugh.

The total cost of the repair was about one million pounds, and the council paid for most of it. Some residents were not happy about the price. A man called Frank Dobbs wrote a letter to the newspaper and said that the money was too much for a small town. But most people think that it was worth it. "A bridge is not only stone," said the mayor, Susan Marlow, at the ceremony. "It joins neighbours, schools and families. Today we are one town again."

At ten o'clock, the mayor cut a red ribbon, and the school band played a cheerful song. The first vehicle to cross was a red bus full of children, and the passengers waved from the windows. Behind it came a line of cars, bicycles and people on foot. Some elderly residents stopped in the middle of the bridge and looked at the river, and a few of them cried. "My grandfather helped to repair this bridge in 1952," said one old woman. "I am glad that it is going to stand for another hundred years."

Some of the older residents remembered the bridge in a different time. In the past, it was a meeting place where people sold fruit and fish on Saturdays. The mayor said that she would like to bring back the weekend market next spring, and several stallholders have already asked for a place.

The council also made some changes. The bridge is now a little wider, so a pavement can be built for pedestrians. There are new lights, and the river wall is higher, which should protect the town from future floods. Engineers say that the bridge is stronger than it was before, and they will check it every year.

For the shopkeepers, the reopening is the best news in months. Linda Okafor says that she is going to make a special cake for the occasion. "It will be in the shape of a bridge," she said. "And the first customer gets a free slice." By lunchtime, there was already a line outside her door. Ashford Green is back in business, and the swans, it seems, are very happy too.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: В конце слога язык оттягивается назад, звук твёрдый. Не произносите мягкое русское «ль».
Губы округлите и вытяните вперёд, зубы не касаются губы. Это не русское «в».
Короткий звук, похожий на «а» без напряжения, рот полуоткрыт.
Звонкие согласные в конце слова (b, d, g, v, z) не оглушайте: say «bed», а не «bet».

questions.question: Why did the council close the bridge?
questions.answer: Heavy rain made the river higher and the stone cracked, so it was too dangerous.

questions.question: How long did the repair take?
Why was there a delay in June?
questions.answer: A family of swans built a nest in the work area, and the workers could not disturb them.

questions.question: What will the bakery owner make?
questions.answer: A special cake in the shape of a bridge.
